Strait of Hormuz Status: October 12, 2026 | Straits Daily Brief
Skip to content Straits Hormuz Live Monitor Day  225 Open? Live map News About Method API Live

Strait of Hormuz · Daily brief · UTC
12 October 2026 .
Brent $ 104.10 -0.59 % · Transits 4 (2026-10-04) · AI-assisted
01 Iranian state media claim a third oil tanker caught fire after striking a sea mine in the Strait of Hormuz, per IRNA; no major wire in this feed carries the claim independently.

02 Brent stood at $104.10 as of 06:12 UTC, down 0.59% over 24 hours; IMF PortWatch recorded 4 transits on October 4, against a pre-crisis baseline of 85 per day.

03 Two Indian seafarers remain missing after a drone struck MT Petro Dolphin, per Maritime Gateway.

Situation
The Strait of Hormuz remains effectively closed to commercial traffic, with tanker strikes continuing across the waterway. Separately, Anadolu Ajansı reports that the IRGC Navy says an oil tanker struck a mine in the strait, and The New York Post and The Hill report that Iran set a supertanker ablaze after US forces disabled a ship breaking the blockade, without identifying who attacked the tanker. UKMTO reported a tanker struck by an unidentified projectile, reported on October 11, per Rudaw, and the crew was reported safe. On the diplomatic front, the lead claim that Iran insists the strait stays shut until the US meets seven conditions is directly contested within the same window: Moneycontrol reports Iran has rejected the US response to those conditions as insufficient, leaving the Iran-US exchange without forward movement. IRNA also claims the IRGC has warned vessels attempting to transit without complying with its regulations. Brent traded at $104.10 as of 06:12 UTC, down 0.59% over 24 hours. IMF PortWatch recorded 4 transits on October 4, against a pre-crisis baseline of 85 per day. As of 06:20 UTC, 112 AIS-visible vessels were holding position away from berth in the Strait of Hormuz and Gulf watch box, a count that leaves out ships within 25km of a working port. On the Hormuz Index, Crisis Pressure, the state composite, sits in the extreme band, flat over 24 hours, with its value set by physical transit deviation alone; the Escalation Forecast sits in the high band, flat over 24 hours, with the Brent-WTI forward spread as its top contributor.
